note: The run. Acts, levels and targets are authored here — nothing generates this file. A level either carries a board, written out as rows of three-character cells (see `parseBoard` in src/board.js, and `node tools/trapBoards.js` to generate one), or deals a board from `width`/`height`/`colors` and a seed, with the act's `mix` saying how much of it has an ability. Run `node tools/makeLevels.js` to check every level is winnable and to choose seeds for the ones that deal; `--write` saves the seeds it picked.

levels.teaches: A glyph landing on its own colour activates
levels.note: Two cells, one possible swap. The player cannot do anything wrong, only the right thing.

levels.teaches: Any two cells swap — they need not touch
levels.note: The board looks full and only the two ends reach each other. A near-miss costs the level.

levels.teaches: A advances the line it points at, and what it pushes lands home
levels.note: The column above the A is grounded so both pieces it moves land matched. The one visible match on the board clears one and loses the level.

levels.teaches: Turned over, it points the other way
levels.note: The same column and the same swap; only the letter is turned.

levels.teaches: On its side it works across
levels.note: Turned again, and the board with it.

levels.teaches: And the other way across
levels.note: The last of the four. By here the rotation should be read without counting.

levels.teaches: O advances all four lines at once
levels.note: Each arm is grounded to land its inner piece matched, so the O pays four times over. Other swaps score one and fall short.

levels.teaches: A line stops at H, and what it stops behind lands home
levels.note: The line is three long and ends at the anchor, so two pieces slide and both land matched.
board: cD> dB. cA. aB. bA. cAH cB.

levels.teaches: + trades above with below, and left with right
levels.note: Every cell in the diamond is grounded for the piece the + sends to it.

levels.teaches: X trades the corners instead
levels.note: The mirror of the + board, on the corners.

levels.teaches: R turns the four around it one step clockwise
levels.note: Four cells, each grounded for the piece the turn brings it. The letters say which way it went.

levels.teaches: Its mirror turns them back
levels.note: The same board the other way, so only the letter decides where each piece lands.

levels.teaches: S opens a hole and everything falls inward
levels.note: Each arm is grounded for the piece the pull brings in.

levels.teaches: A glyph on its own colour activates
levels.note: At two colours every glyph is the opposite of its cell, so every swap that lands at all is a double hit. The player cannot fail to see the rule.

levels.teaches: You move glyphs, not cells
levels.note: Same trivial palette, so attention is on what moved. The ground stays put and the shape travels.

levels.teaches: Any two cells swap — the whole board is in reach
levels.note: Put the only two useful pieces in opposite corners. A rule taught by letting the move work is cheaper than one taught by refusing it.

levels.teaches: A swap can miss, and the board drains
levels.note: The third colour is where choosing begins — two openings in three now pay once instead of twice, and a wasted swap costs the target.

levels.teaches: Activating advances every line around it
levels.note: One O in an otherwise inert board. The player should see exactly four things move, and nothing else.

levels.teaches: A shoved glyph can land on its own colour — the chain
levels.note: Author the board so the first pulse hands the player a second match it did not have to look for.

levels.teaches: A line runs until it meets a sink
levels.note: The front piece falls off the board edge. Show the whole line move and one piece leave.

levels.teaches: The board drains, and the budget bites
levels.note: Fifth colour. A pulse that hits nothing is now the expensive mistake.

levels.teaches: Set the chain up before you fire it
levels.note: The first level whose target is out of reach without arranging one pulse to feed another.

levels.teaches: A pointed glyph advances one line, the way it points
levels.note: Four A's, one of each facing, in an otherwise inert board. The drawing is the only thing saying which way it goes.

levels.teaches: Which one you trigger is the choice
levels.note: Two pointed glyphs whose lines cross. Only one order clears the target.

levels.teaches: Aim into a hole an earlier shove opened
levels.note: The board cannot offer this until pieces have left it. Author a line that only works second.

levels.teaches: Two aims that meet
levels.note: Opposed pushes on the same line — the pieces between them have nowhere to go.

levels.teaches: Direction beats force
levels.note: Full palette. A pulse would waste three of its four lines here; the pointed glyph spends nothing.

levels.teaches: An anchor eats the front of any line that reaches it
levels.note: One anchor at the end of a long line. The player should watch a piece arrive and simply stop existing.

levels.teaches: An anchor is a sink you can aim into
levels.note: The brake used on purpose: the only line that clears the target is the one pointed at the wall.

levels.teaches: A line boxed between two anchors
levels.note: Nothing leaves. Everything shuffles. The player has to spend the space rather than the pieces.

levels.teaches: The board you cannot drain
levels.note: Full palette and enough anchors that the rim stops helping. The target is met by choosing, not by clearing.

levels.teaches: Some glyphs rearrange instead of clearing
levels.note: One + in an inert board. Four pieces move, nothing leaves, and the count does not go up — yet.

levels.teaches: A trade can make a match that was not there
levels.note: Author the two cells either side of a + so that exchanging them lands both on their own colour.

levels.teaches: The cross trades edges, the ex trades corners
levels.note: Both on one board, each the wrong tool for the other's job.

levels.teaches: Trade first, fire second
levels.note: Full palette. The target needs a + to set up a pulse, in that order and no other.

levels.teaches: The ring turns one step
levels.note: One R. North's piece ends up east, east's south, and so on round. Nothing leaves the board.

levels.teaches: Turn it back
levels.note: R and its mirror on one board. The same four cells, the other way round — the player has to read which is which.

levels.teaches: The sink pulls inward and takes its own cell
levels.note: The last level. S draws all four lines in and dies first, so the hole it leaves is the sink they run into.
